collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager admits taking a neighbor's net: ask for an apology, or ask them to make it right.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has admitted, ashamed, that (subject.he/she) took (friend)'s fishing net when (subject.his/her) own tore, and lost it at sea. (friend) needs a net to feed (friend.his/her) family. The village is waiting to see what (friend) asks for. What should (friend) ask?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) accepts (subject)'s apology. It is sincere. It does not catch fish. (friend)'s family eats less for a month, until (friend) can weave a new net. (friend) is glad (friend.he/she) was kind, and also hungry.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks (subject) to weave a new net and to fish for (friend)'s family until it is done. (subject) does both. It is hard, and fair. By the end, the two of them fish together sometimes.
